resolutions.researcher_notes: Original ref (saymar.org PDF) is effectively dead: URL returns 200 but no longer contains gas-pipeline content ('غاز' absent); no Wayback capture (404). Found NO source stating the project is 'shelved'. On the contrary, the live seed source (Independent Arabia, 2021-01-19) presents it as an active government project: construction approved 2019 and work 'nearing completion' as of Jan 2021 — this CONTRADICTS the 'shelved' status. Status left unresolved/dead; flag the discrepancy for the status-sweep — GEM may have been reclassified to shelved on later info I could not locate.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) states the Iraqi government approved/adopted the project in 2019 ('the Iraqi government approved construction in 2019'), supporting ProposalYear 2019. Single independent source → medium. Verified page contains '2019' and 'الرميلة الشمالية'/'النجف'/'وزارة النفط'. No second independent source found; story appears unique to Independent Arabia.

Same Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) article: government approved construction in 2019 and work was 'nearing completion' as of Jan 2021, consistent with ConstructionYear 2019. Single source → medium. Note: the article does not cleanly separate proposal vs. construction-start dates — 2019 is the approval/start year it gives.

Could not corroborate Capacity 258 MMSCMD. Original saymar.org PDF is dead; no Wayback. Independent Arabia article (verified live) does NOT contain '258' and gives only a downstream electrical figure ('more than 2,500 MW'), not a gas throughput. The '258' figure appears to trace to the related Basra–Aqaba/Iraq–Jordan project (2b1stconsulting: 350 MMSCFD within Iraq / 258 MMSCFD within Jordan, and note the unit there is MMSCFD not MMSCMD) — likely a cross-project/unit mis-derivation. Left unresolved; flag possible bad value+unit.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) explicitly: 'أنبوب يبلغ طوله أكثر من 350 كيلو متراً من حقول الرميلة الشمالية' (a pipeline more than 350 km long from the North Rumaila fields). Directly corroborates LengthKnown 350 km. Verified page contains both '350' and 'كم'. Single independent source → medium; no second source surfaced despite EN+AR searches.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) states the pipeline draws gas from the North Rumaila oil fields ('من حقول الرميلة الشمالية'), corroborating FuelSource = Rumela. Verified page contains 'الرميلة الشمالية'. Single independent source → medium.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) describes the line running from the North Rumaila fields (Basra governorate) to a chain of cities extending toward Najaf, corroborating Start = Rumela/Basrah, End = Al-Najaf. Verified page contains 'الرميلة الشمالية', 'البصرة', and 'النجف'. Single independent source → medium.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) frames this as a state Ministry of Oil ('وزارة النفط') project managed by the state Basra Oil Company (with Basrah Gas Company/Shell on gas ops). Supports Owner1 = Iraq Ministry of Oil, 100% (state). Verified page contains 'وزارة النفط'. Minor nuance: the immediate implementing entity named is Basra Oil Company (a state company under the Ministry) — consistent with MoO ownership. Single independent source → medium. The Shell 'Basrah Gas Company' seed page verified live but does NOT mention Najaf/this pipeline, so it is not usable here.
